# autoharness-lock.txt
#
# Hash-pinned constraints for the `autoharness` CI install
# (.github/workflows/ci.yml, topology-check job). Resolves stash EFFAA358
# (007.001-T / U1).
#
# WHY THIS EXISTS: the previous `pip install autoharness` was a FLOATING,
# unhashed install. It re-resolved the latest release and its transitive
# dependency graph on every CI run with no verification that the fetched
# bytes matched anything previously audited — a compromised PyPI account,
# mutable index, or MITM'd transitive dependency could execute arbitrary
# code in the runner. `pip install --require-hashes -r <this file>` closes
# that: every package (autoharness itself AND its full transitive closure)
# is pinned to an exact version AND verified against a committed SHA-256
# hash before pip will install it. A hash mismatch or an unlisted
# transitive dependency fails the install instead of silently proceeding.
#
# RESOLUTION PROVENANCE: versions/hashes below were resolved on
# 2026-09-04 via:
#   pip download autoharness==1.4.11 \
#     --platform manylinux_2_17_x86_64 --python-version 312 \
#     --implementation cp --abi cp312 --only-binary=:all: -d <scratch>
#   pip hash <each wheel>
# `--platform manylinux_2_17_x86_64 --python-version 312 --abi cp312`
# targets the exact runtime this install runs under today: ubuntu-latest +
# `actions/setup-python` `python-version: '3.12'` (see the `topology-check`
# job above). 1.4.11 was PyPI's latest release for `autoharness` at
# resolution time (`pip index versions autoharness` reported
# `LATEST: 1.4.11`), i.e. the same version the prior floating install
# would have resolved on a clean runner — this pin reproduces, not changes,
# CI's current behavior.
#
# MAINTENANCE: version bumps are deliberate, not automatic. To bump:
#   1. Resolve the new target version and re-run the two pip commands above
#      against THIS repo's CI runtime (ubuntu-latest + the Python version
#      pinned in ci.yml's `actions/setup-python` step for this job).
#   2. Regenerate every hash below for the new full transitive closure —
#      do not hand-edit hashes, and do not carry forward a stale hash for
#      an unchanged-looking dependency (transitive wheels can be rebuilt
#      with the same version string).
#   3. Never float (`autoharness` with no `==`, or any dependency added
#      without a matching `--hash=sha256:...`) — `--require-hashes`
#      enforces this at install time, but do not attempt to work around it.
#
# [Historical: originally resolved for autoharness==1.4.11 below; see the
# CORRECTION note further down -- the ACTIVE pin is autoharness==1.5.0.]
# Full transitive closure for cp312-manylinux_2_17 (8 packages total;
# verified as the complete resolved set via a REAL Python 3.12
# interpreter's native resolver -- see "REMEDIATION" note below -- no
# additional dependency introduced silently by a future run of this same
# install).
#
# REMEDIATION (adversarial re-review, 2026-09-04): the original 7-package
# closure recorded here was resolved via
# `pip download --platform ... --python-version 312 --implementation cp
# --abi cp312`, a CROSS-PLATFORM/CROSS-VERSION resolve mode. That mode was
# independently found (by two adversarial reviewers, one with a
# reproduction) to NOT fully evaluate PEP 508 environment markers the same
# way a native resolve does: `referencing==0.37.0` declares
# `typing-extensions>=4.4.0; python_version < "3.13"`, which is a REAL,
# mandatory requirement under Python 3.12 (the exact version `ci.yml`
# pins) but was silently omitted from the cross-platform resolve's output.
# Confirmed against a REAL local Python 3.12.10 interpreter
# (`pip install --dry-run` with no platform override, native resolver):
# `typing-extensions` IS collected and IS part of "Would install". Added
# below with its own verified hash. `pip install --require-hashes -r
# <this file>` was re-run afterward against the corrected 8-package set
# targeting manylinux_2_17_x86_64/cp312 and now succeeds.

# CORRECTION (CI failure, 2026-09-05): the version above (1.4.11) was
# WRONG. It was resolved via this sandbox's `pip`, which is configured
# (`pip config list` -> `global.index-url=https://packagefeedproxy.microsoft.io/pypi/simple/`)
# to use an INTERNAL package proxy whose view of "latest" was stale
# relative to the REAL public PyPI that GitHub-hosted `ubuntu-latest`
# runners actually resolve against (no proxy, direct public internet).
# The prior floating `pip install autoharness` on the real CI runner had
# been resolving `autoharness==1.5.0` all along (confirmed directly from
# this repo's own last-known-good CI job log, and independently from
# `https://pypi.org/pypi/autoharness/json` queried directly), NOT 1.4.11.
# Pinning to 1.4.11 was therefore not "reproducing CI's current behavior"
# (U1 AC-3) — it silently downgraded the runtime and broke
# `ci-topology-check.sh`, which calls `autoharness gate pipeline-topology`,
# a subcommand that does not exist in 1.4.11 (added after 1.4.11, present
# in 1.5.0). CI on this PR caught this immediately (`Unknown gate
# subcommand: pipeline-topology`, exit 2).
#
# Fixed: `autoharness` bumped to `1.5.0` with its official PyPI-published
# SHA-256 digest (fetched directly from
# `https://pypi.org/pypi/autoharness/1.5.0/json` -> `urls[].digests.sha256`
# for the `py3-none-any` wheel — this environment's direct HTTPS access to
# `files.pythonhosted.org` for the actual wheel bytes is itself blocked by
# the same sandbox network policy, but PyPI's own JSON metadata API,
# reachable directly, publishes the authoritative digest PyPI computed at
# upload time; no separate download-and-hash step was needed or possible
# here). `autoharness==1.5.0`'s `requires_dist` (`jsonschema>=4.23.0`,
# `pyyaml>=6.0.2`) is IDENTICAL to `1.4.11`'s, and this repo's own
# most-recent successful main-branch CI run (the last floating install
# before this shipment) already recorded the exact resolved transitive
# closure on the real runner: `attrs-26.1.0`, `jsonschema-4.26.0`,
# `jsonschema-specifications-2025.9.1`, `pyyaml-6.0.3`, `referencing-0.37.0`,
# `rpds-py-2026.6.3`, `typing-extensions-4.16.0` — the SAME 7 versions
# already recorded below (unchanged; only the `autoharness` entry itself
# needed correction). LESSON FOR FUTURE BUMPS: always cross-check a
# resolved version/hash against the real `https://pypi.org/pypi/<name>/json`
# (or an actual GitHub Actions CI log) before trusting any locally
# configured package index/proxy — a corporate mirror's freshness is not
# guaranteed to match what the public CI runner will actually fetch.
#
# Full transitive closure of `autoharness==1.5.0` for cp312-manylinux_2_17
# (8 packages total; verified as the complete resolved set via a REAL
# Python 3.12 interpreter's native resolver -- see "REMEDIATION" note below
# -- no additional dependency introduced silently by a future run of this
# same install).
#
# REMEDIATION (adversarial re-review, 2026-09-04): the original 7-package
# closure recorded here was resolved via
# `pip download --platform ... --python-version 312 --implementation cp
# --abi cp312`, a CROSS-PLATFORM/CROSS-VERSION resolve mode. That mode was
# independently found (by two adversarial reviewers, one with a
# reproduction) to NOT fully evaluate PEP 508 environment markers the same
# way a native resolve does: `referencing==0.37.0` declares
# `typing-extensions>=4.4.0; python_version < "3.13"`, which is a REAL,
# mandatory requirement under Python 3.12 (the exact version `ci.yml`
# pins) but was silently omitted from the cross-platform resolve's output.
# Confirmed against a REAL local Python 3.12.10 interpreter
# (`pip install --dry-run` with no platform override, native resolver):
# `typing-extensions` IS collected and IS part of "Would install". Added
# below with its own verified hash. `pip install --require-hashes -r
# <this file>` was re-run afterward against the corrected 8-package set
# targeting manylinux_2_17_x86_64/cp312 and now succeeds.

autoharness==1.5.0 \
    --hash=sha256:720049ceb1731b01168cd455c2d36babe7743de890b0ce05a840353a52424282
attrs==26.1.0 \
    --hash=sha256:c647aa4a12dfbad9333ca4e71fe62ddc36f4e63b2d260a37a8b83d2f043ac309
jsonschema==4.26.0 \
    --hash=sha256:d489f15263b8d200f8387e64b4c3a75f06629559fb73deb8fdfb525f2dab50ce
jsonschema-specifications==2025.9.1 \
    --hash=sha256:98802fee3a11ee76ecaca44429fda8a41bff98b00a0f2838151b113f210cc6fe
pyyaml==6.0.3 \
    --hash=sha256:ba1cc08a7ccde2d2ec775841541641e4548226580ab850948cbfda66a1befcdc
referencing==0.37.0 \
    --hash=sha256:381329a9f99628c9069361716891d34ad94af76e461dcb0335825aecc7692231
rpds-py==2026.6.3 \
    --hash=sha256:ecabd69db66de867690f9797f2f8fa27ba501bbc24540cbdbdc649cd15888ba6
typing-extensions==4.16.0 \
    --hash=sha256:481caa481374e813c1b176ada14e97f1f67a4539ce9cfeb3f350d78d6370c2e8
